results.name: Blue Dinosaur (Rigged)
results.description: Stylized character inspired by a stegosaurus baby. Stegosaurus was a large herbivorous dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (about 150 million years ago) in North America. Its name comes from the distinctive flat plates on its back and tail, which may have served for thermoregulation or display. It grew up to 9 m long and weighed around 4–7 tons, with some estimates even higher. It had a brain the size of a mandarin, short front legs, and hind legs about twice as long. Its tail ended with four long spikes, used as an effective defense against predators, as shown by injuries found on Allosaurus bones. Stegosaurs were slow (walking speed about 6–7 km/h). The most famous and best-preserved skeleton, nicknamed “Sophie,” is on display at the Natural History Museum in London.

results.name: Toy Balance Scale
results.description: This handcrafted wooden balance scale is a vibrant study in primary and secondary colors, featuring a sturdy base and upright support finished in a bright red and orange. The horizontal balance beam is left as natural wood, showcasing a clean grain that highlights the mechanical pivot point, while the two suspended weighing pans pop in a cheerful yellow. Three graduated wooden weights sit nestled in the pans, their sizes clearly indicating a hierarchy of mass, while the remaining two weights are tucked neatly into custom-fit cutout recesses carved directly into the scale's base for storage. The interplay between the colorful painted surfaces and the raw timber beam creates a classic educational aesthetic that feels both playful and precision-engineered.

results.name: Triceratops (Rigged)
results.description: The name Triceratops means “three-horned face,” and in real life it was anything but small. This massive four-legged herbivore could grow up to around 8–9 meters long and weigh several tons. It lived in western North America at the very end of the Late Cretaceous, about 68–66 million years ago, making it one of the last non-avian dinosaurs before the mass extinction. One of its most distinctive features was its enormous skull, among the largest known for any land vertebrate, equipped with three impressive horns and a solid bony frill. Those features may have helped with defense, display, or both. Triceratops was also a highly successful and widespread ceratopsian, and it likely moved in herds.

results.name: Bradden Storage TV Stand
results.description: Upgrade your living room with this sleek storage TV stand that's both functional and stylish. Crafted from a mix of solid and engineered wood, this stand accommodates TVs up to 85'' wide and features mirrored accents that add a touch of glam to your space. With two full-extension drawers on each side, you'll have ample storage for remotes, game controllers, and more. Its 80 lbs. weight capacity ensures it can handle your entertainment setup with ease. Just add your favourite TV and enjoy movie nights or binge-watching sessions in style.
